findings: The new page uses `availablepaymentmethodschange` with a `paymentMethods` payload and React `onAvailablePaymentMethodsChange` to detect current wallet availability (new lines 316-318, 320-374); old guidance used `ready` with `availablePaymentMethods` and React `onReady` (old lines 301-361). Current source lines 75-87, Stripe index lines 65 and 771, and concept lines 20, 69-80, and 148 still teach or advertise the older callback. All these routes need a dated availability-pattern update, without claiming that `ready` was removed for every purpose or version.

The browser table changes Firefox Apple Pay from unsupported (old line 62) to supported subject to the non-Safari desktop `always` option (new lines 67,79). The old footnote restricted desktop Chromium Apple Pay to macOS (old line 74); the new footnote does not repeat that operating-system restriction. Source lines 36-43 need the Firefox correction and should mark the macOS-only statement as dated and unverified pending separate platform evidence. Concept line 35 needs the Firefox correction. The new omission does not establish Windows, Linux, or all-desktop Apple Pay support.

A detailed webview table replaces the older blanket limited-support warning. New lines 83-96 say Apple Pay can work in eligible iOS webviews and Google Pay can work if no popup is needed and, in Android webviews, the host app supports Payment Request API; Link, PayPal, Klarna, and Amazon Pay are marked unsupported. Browser and standard payment-method eligibility still apply. Source line 43 and concept lines 35-37 need this qualified matrix, not a universal webview unsupported claim.

The new page explicitly allows custom payment method buttons via `customPaymentMethods` on `stripe.elements()` (new line 55) and describes Dashboard `cpmt_` ID and `handleRender` error conditions (new line 312), whereas old line 289 said methods could not be specified. The existing concept lines 10 and 155-159 already record a beta typed surface from a separate versioned source; reconcile the dated product-page statement without inferring universal account eligibility, production rollout, or a runtime test.

The six built-in wallets, supported-browser/currency/customer setup gates, domain registration, layout, button types/themes, and fallback advice remain. Code formatting, table separators, sandbox wording, and the agent-directed introductory/CLI text are not independent evidence of a functioning integration and do not authorize any tool or account operation.
substantive_changes: Availability-detection example changed from `ready`/`availablePaymentMethods` to `availablepaymentmethodschange`/`paymentMethods`, including React prop and element-object examples.

Firefox Apple Pay table cell changed to supported with the non-Safari desktop `always` condition; the old macOS-only restriction is absent from the new footnote, but its absence does not establish all-operating-system eligibility.
Specific in-app webview method support and constraints replaced a general limited-support warning.
Custom payment method button support and its `cpmt_`/Dashboard/`handleRender` conditions are now stated on this overview page.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the 2026-04-21 capture's `ready` availability example as dated historical guidance, while describing the November capture's different event as its current recommendation across source, both Stripe index entries, and concept; do not assert API removal or exact SDK-version behavior from this page alone.

Treat the old macOS-only footnote as historical and the new footnote as non-Safari desktop `always` guidance; seek separate platform evidence before asserting that the older operating-system constraint was repealed or that additional desktop systems are supported.
Preserve the six built-in wallets and the distinction between built-in methods and account-qualified custom method buttons.
Retain browser, currency, customer setup, domain, and iframe eligibility gates and the mobile SDK alternative, even where the new support matrix is more specific.
conflicts: Current source lines 75-87, Stripe index lines 65 and 771, and concept lines 20, 69-80, and 148 present or advertise `ready`/`availablePaymentMethods` as the availability callback; new raw lines 316-374 show `availablepaymentmethodschange`/`paymentMethods`.

Current source lines 36-43 and concept line 35 say Firefox Apple Pay is unsupported, contradicting new raw lines 67 and 79. The source also repeats old raw line 74's macOS-only desktop condition, which new raw line 79 omits; qualify that condition as dated/unverified rather than claiming the new capture disproves it on all operating systems.

Current source line 43 and concept lines 35-37 reduce all in-app webviews to limited or no support; new raw lines 83-96 distinguish eligible Apple Pay and Google Pay webviews from four unsupported methods.

Current source lines 68-74 omit custom payment method button support now stated in new raw lines 55 and 301-312; concept lines 155-159 describe a beta typed surface and an older product-documentation limitation, requiring dated evidence reconciliation rather than a broad runtime-availability claim.
unresolved_questions: This captured overview does not establish which account cohorts have custom payment method access, whether the beta typed surface has a general runtime rollout, or whether a particular `cpmt_` ID renders successfully.
The page does not identify exact Stripe.js or React package versions for the event transition, nor prove the `ready` event itself is deprecated or removed.
The newer non-Safari desktop Apple Pay footnote drops the old macOS condition but does not independently establish support on every desktop operating system.
